events.text: The Seattle site began brewing beer.
Rainier was founded.
The brewery was closed by Pabst.
The green T was removed by Tullys.
A red neon replica R returned to the top of the brewery.
A.B. Rabbeson opened Washington Brewery, Seattle's first commercial brewing company.
Rabbeson renamed his brewery Seattle Brewery.
The brewery launched Rainier beer.
John Kopp and Andrew Hemrich founded Seattle Brewing and Malting.
Rabbeson sold his brewery and the Rainier brand to Kopp and Hemrich.
Kopp and Hemrich stopped producing Rainier beer in Washington due to the state's prohibition.
The company stopped brewing Rainier beer in San Francisco when the 18th amendment was ratified.
The company began brewing Rainier beer.
The brewery began operating under names such as Sicks Seattle Brewing and Malting and Sicks Rainier Brewing Company.
The period of using names like Sicks Seattle Brewing and Malting and Sicks Rainier Brewing Company ended.
The branch brewery in Spokane closed.
Rainier began being packaged in a series of decorative beer cans known as the Rainier Jubilee Series.
The Rainier Jubilee Series of decorative beer cans ended.
A set of Christmas cans were marketed as the first in the Jubilee Series.
Christmas cans were marketed again.
Rainier and other brands began losing market share to major national brands.
Rainier and other brands began losing market share to major national brands.
Rainier ran a number of memorable television ads in the Pacific Northwest.
A commercial ad featuring a motorcycle revving Rainier Beer was notable.
A commercial ad featuring a motorcycle revving Rainier Beer was notable.
The brewery was sold to G. Heileman Brewing Company.
Pabst Brewing Company closed the brewery.
The Olympia Brewing Company closed.
Sleeman Breweries acquired Stroh Canada and became the Canadian manufacturer and distributor of Rainier.
Rainier was awarded a silver medal by the Great American Beer Festival in the category of Best American Light Lager.
The Great American Beer Festival awarded Rainier a gold medal for Best American-Style Lager.
The Great American Beer Festival awarded Rainier a gold medal for Best American-Style Lager.
The Great American Beer Festival awarded Rainier a gold medal for Best American-Style Lager.
Rainier received a silver medal in the Best American-Style Lager category from the Great American Beer Festival.
Rainier received a silver medal in the Best American-Style Lager category from the Great American Beer Festival.
The red Rainier R logo dates back to the 1900s.
The company adopted the current R logo since the 1950s.
The logo contained a baseball style word mark shown in early 1900s advertisements.
The baseball style word mark was used up until the 1950s.
A large red neon R logo sign was created and placed atop the brewery.
Tullys replaced the iconic R with a green neon Tullys T sign after leasing the brewery.
Tullys decided to replace the green T with a replica of the red R sign.
The green T sign was removed.
The new red R sign was installed.
Rainier beer appears in the film Stand By Me.
The band Mudhoney was photographed with cans of Rainier Beer.
Rainier beer appears in the film Twilight.
A black bear consumed 36 cans of Rainier beer in Baker Lake, Washington.
The television series Longmire features the main character exclusively drinking Rainier beer.
